variants.reason: Approved template reads 'located in the {GAO_MG_METER_LOCATION}. {CONDITION_OK_GAS_SMELL} and no visible evidence of leakage or other significant defects...'. Two verified reductions apply when the gas-smell checkbox IS checked (so the optional smell-clause sub-phrase is empty): (1) the location dropdown options are pre-worded full predicates that already supply their own preposition ('under the stairs', 'in an outside box') - combining both would read 'located in the under the stairs', so the handler strips the template's fixed 'in the '; (2) with the smell clause empty, the template would leave a dangling lowercase 'and' right after the location sentence's full stop ('...stairs. and no visible evidence...') - the handler turns this into its own capitalised sentence ('...stairs. No visible evidence...'), replacing the literal word 'and' with 'No' rather than emitting a fragment. The dangling-and cleanup string in the handler was updated in lockstep with this Phase 2D wording change (previously matched the pre-L2 'no other defects' phrasing).

variants.reason:
Harness compiler bug, not an app defect: the approved bank text for this key is TWO sentences joined by a single ' ' (no '

' double-break). The app's own _split() only breaks phrases on double-newline/'

' boundaries, so it correctly keeps both sentences as ONE phrase entry (matching the bank's own single-vs-double-break convention). But loadApprovedBank()'s compile() step splits templates on ANY ' '/'
' occurrence (single included) to get fine-grained matchers for other multi-line masters, which shreds this specific template into two independently-anchored regexes that can never match the combined single-string output. Verified by reading the raw phrase_texts.json value directly (both sentences present, single ' ' separator) - the app is emitting the bank text byte-for-byte. Fixing the general splitter would risk breaking match granularity elsewhere (already ruled out reworking it once in Phase 4b), so this specific combined form is captured as its own variant instead.
